questions.question: Which punctuation mark completes the sentence correctly? — 'I love pizza___'
Choose the correct sentence.
options: She bought apples bananas and oranges.
She bought apples, bananas, and oranges.
She bought, apples, bananas and oranges.
She bought apples, bananas and, oranges.
questions.answer: She bought apples, bananas, and oranges.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
options: I was tired; but I couldn’t sleep.
I was tired; I couldn’t sleep.
I was tired, I couldn’t sleep.
I was tired: I couldn’t sleep.
questions.answer: I was tired; I couldn’t sleep.

questions.question: Which punctuation mark introduces a list?
Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: It’s raining—don’t forget your umbrella!
It’s raining, don’t forget your umbrella!
It’s raining; don’t forget your umbrella.
It’s raining: don’t forget your umbrella!

questions.question: Which sentence uses parentheses correctly?
options: My brother (who lives in Spain) is coming to visit.
My brother) who lives in Spain (is coming to visit.
My brother who lives in Spain) is coming to visit (.
My brother (who lives in Spain is coming to visit).
questions.answer: My brother (who lives in Spain) is coming to visit.

questions.question: Which punctuation mark is missing? — 'Where are you___'
Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: Wow! That was amazing!
Wow? That was amazing.
Wow, that was amazing!
Wow; that was amazing!

questions.question: Which punctuation mark is used to show possession?
options: Apostrophe (')
Comma (,)
Colon (:)
Dash (—)

questions.question: Choose the correct use of quotation marks.
options: He said, “I’ll be there soon.”
He said, “I’ll be there soon”.
He said “I’ll be there soon”.
He said, I’ll be there soon.
